title: Bandit Slots
subtitle: Multi-Armed Bandit Problem
overview: A row of slot machines, each with unknown payout rates. The challenge: find the best machine while minimizing losses from testing bad ones.
rules: Each machine has a hidden payout probability
You don't know which machine is best
Balance exploring new machines vs exploiting known good ones
Goal: maximize total winnings over time

algorithm.name: Epsilon-Greedy & Softmax
algorithm.description: e-Greedy randomly explores with probability e, otherwise picks the best-known option. Softmax assigns probabilities proportional to estimated values.

proof.explanation: Regret measures the cost of not knowing which arm is optimal.
steps: Let delta_a = q*(a*) - q*(a) be the suboptimality gap
Expected regret from pulling suboptimal arm a is delta_a
e-greedy explores with probability e, exploits with 1-e
Regret grows as O(sqrt(T)), not O(T) - sublinear!
proof.conclusion: Sublinear regret means average regret per round goes to zero.

proof.explanation: The fundamental dilemma: try new options or stick with what seems best?
proof.formula: Explore: Gain information, risk short-term loss. Exploit: Use knowledge, risk missing better option.
steps: Pure exploitation: May never find the best arm
Pure exploration: Never uses learned information
Softmax: Probability proportional to estimated value
proof.conclusion: Some exploration is always needed. Balance short-term cost vs long-term gain.

keyInsight: This is the fundamental exploration-exploitation dilemma in AI.
